programme.title: Shark
programme.desc: A look at how an international team of scientists is trying to change people's perceptions of sharks. Their research is revealing that sharks can be sociable and intelligent, and they could even help solve some of the toughest medical challenges of the 21st century. However, the breakthroughs come at a time when many sharks face extinction. Science may now be the only way to save them.

programme.title: Pubs, Ponds and Power: The Story of the Village
programme.desc: Archaeologist Ben Robinson explores Lavenham in Suffolk, the best-preserved medieval village in the country. In the 16th century, Lavenham was one of the wealthiest places in England, becoming rich on its woollen cloth industry, but the industry declined and the wealthy abandoned Lavenham. By the 19th century it was a place of poverty, but today it is once more a jewel of a village.

programme.title: Canals: The Making of a Nation
programme.desc: Presenter Liz McIvor tells the story of the people who operated the canal boats carrying fuel and goods around the country. Conditions were tough, days were long. Victorian society began to grow suspicious of these 'outsiders', and they gained reputations for criminality, violence and drinking. But was this really deserved? Liz discovers grisly canal crimes, investigates health and welfare onboard working boats, and looks at why canal children were last on the list to be offered safeguards and formal education. The Victorians eventually championed the needs of children who were forced to labour in factories and mines, but the boat children were often ignored. Liz discovers the campaigners who set out to tackle this injustice, including George Smith of Coalville, Leicestershire, and Sister Mary Ward of Stoke Bruerne.

programme.desc: Relive the biggest and best moments from an unforgettable weekend as Radio 2 in the Park made its Scottish debut in spectacular Stirling. Expect huge performances from the likes of Deacon Blue, Appleton, Blue, Cast, James Blunt, Level 42, Texas, Lulu, Jack Savoretti, ABC, The Script, Emeli Sandé and this year’s headliners, the 'queen of funk’ Chaka Khan and local legends Simple Minds, as we celebrate a spectacular two days of incredible live music.

programme.title: The Rolling Stones: Live at the Fonda
programme.desc: This programme captures a truly unique event in the long and eventful history of The Rolling Stones. On 20 May 2015, at the Fonda Theatre in Hollywood, the band performed the entire Sticky Fingers album live in concert for the first, and so far only time, in their career. The show celebrated the reissue of the Sticky Fingers album and was the opening night of the band's Zip Code Tour of North America that would run over the next two months. The intimate setting of the Fonda Theatre was in contrast to the huge stadiums in which the band would perform for the rest of the tour and made this an incredibly special occasion for those fans lucky enough to get a ticket.

programme.title: My Life as a Rolling Stone
programme.desc: Mick Jagger has spent 60 years as frontman for The Rolling Stones. In this documentary, he talks exclusively about his life in the band, from his first performances in local teenage parties to his creation of a stage persona that has defined the rock 'n' roll lead singer, making Jagger a global icon and musical visionary. Featuring vivid archive footage from his astonishing career, a rich soundtrack of Stones classic tracks and interviews with a stellar cast of musicians and those close to the band.

programme.title: My Life as a Rolling Stone
programme.desc: Ronnie Wood is a cultural icon, guitar hero, artist and the living embodiment of the vibrancy of British-born rock 'n' roll. In this documentary, Ronnie talks exclusively about his career in music and his life as a Rolling Stone, with its exhilarating highs and sometimes dangerous lows. Through vivid archive footage, brilliant music and interviews with a stellar cast of musicians, the film reveals how he binds the band together through his musical virtuosity and his irresistible, positive personality.

programme.title: Simon King's Shetland Adventure
programme.desc: Simon King, wildlife cameraman and Springwatch presenter, sets off on an adventure to live on the Shetland Islands with his family through the changing seasons. Simon has travelled the world for 30 years, but his boyhood dream was to visit Shetland. Now he has the chance to film some of the remarkable wildlife and experience the beauty and the wild weather of Britain's most northerly isles. Simon captures footage of killer whales coming in to kill a seal, an Arctic tern colony attacked by a bonxie, and a shy otter family. Simon, his wife Marguerite and two-year-old daughter Savannah settle into a remote cottage, but the winter weather and winds of over 100mph make life tough for them. To celebrate winter, Simon joins the local Shetlanders in their Viking Up Helly Aa festivals, but there is a surprise for him: he is asked to come in drag, dressed as fellow Springwatch presenter Kate Humble. This doesn't stop him enjoying himself or helping to set light to a Viking boat in a genuine Shetland experience.

programme.title: Life on Earth
programme.desc: David Attenborough looks for crucial clues that help to explain how and why we have come to dominate life on earth. He traces back the African origins of humans to nearly three million years ago, and along the way he goes into caves in southern France where Stone Age people created imaginative paintings of ice-age animals. He also travels to Papua New Guinea to find some hunter-gatherers who have never before set eyes on white people.

programme.title: Paris Police
programme.desc: Meg Steinheil is discovered bound and gagged, with the bodies of both her husband and mother found nearby. Commissaire Cochefert and Detective Jouin are suspicious of her witness statement. Prefect Lepine attends the laying-in ceremony of Emile Zola at the Pantheon and tells his men to do whatever is necessary to dispel the protesters inflamed at the presence of Alfred Dreyfus. In French with English subtitles.

programme.title: Paris Police
programme.desc: A torn-up card provides police with a lead in the case of the Steinheil home invasion, but their resources are stretched when a gunman attempts to assassinate Alfred Dreyfus. Journalist Marcel Hutin ingratiates himself with Jouin, who provides him with a copy of Adolphe Steinheil's autopsy report. In French with English subtitles.

programme.title: Scrublands
programme.desc: At the end of a long book-signing tour, Martin Scarsden hopes for a peaceful holiday with his partner Mandy Bond, who is already staying at the local yoga retreat in his home town of Port Silver. programme.title: Scrublands
programme.desc: As Martin continues to investigate the events surrounding the murder of his friend Jasper, he and Mandy learn that someone at Hummingbird Beach retreat had spiked her drink. In town, Martin bumps into his uncle Vernon and has pangs of guilt about an old betrayal.

programme.title: To the Manor Born

programme.title: Keeping Up Appearances

programme.title: Shark
programme.desc: A look at how an international team of scientists is trying to change people's perceptions of sharks. Their research is revealing that sharks can be sociable and intelligent, and they could even help solve some of the toughest medical challenges of the 21st century. However, the breakthroughs come at a time when many sharks face extinction. Science may now be the only way to save them.

programme.title: Crossing England in a Punt: River of Dreams
programme.desc: From the Staffordshire hills to the Humber estuary, spirited explorer Tom Fort embarks on a 170-mile journey down Britain's third-longest river, the Trent. Beginning on foot, he soon transfers to his own custom-built punt, the Trent Otter, and rows many miles downstream. Along the way he encounters the power stations that generate much of the nation's electricity, veterans of the catastrophic floods of 1947, the 19th-century brewers of Burton and a Bronze Age boatman who once made a life along the river.

programme.title: A Wild Year
programme.desc: Hidden away in the most easterly part of the British Isles are the Fens of East Anglia, a landscape of big skies and distant horizons, wild wetlands and fertile farmland. Water has always been the driving force here - its ebb and flow has shaped the Fens for thousands of years. The ancient wetlands covered hundreds of square miles and overflowed with wildlife. Today, well over 90% has gone, drained over the centuries and converted into farmland. Yet despite these changes, it is still possible to glimpse the richness of those wetlands. Every winter, thousands of migrating whooper swans return to the flooded pastures of the Ouse washes from their Arctic breeding grounds. Here, they join thousands of other waterfowl in one of Britain’s greatest wildlife gatherings. On the Welney Wetlands, spring sees ‘mad’ march hares boxing over mates. It was once thought these bouts were male hares boxing for dominance, but it is often the females throwing the punches to fend off the attentions of over-eager suitors.

programme.title: The Riviera: A History in Pictures
programme.desc: Two-part series in which Richard E Grant follows in the footsteps of artists who have lived, loved and painted on France's glorious Cote d'Azur. Revealing the intertwined relationship between modern art and the development of the French Riviera as an international tourist haven, Grant explores how impressionist painters Cezanne, Monet and Renoir first discovered the region in the 19th century, when the newly built railway arrived there. Captivated by the light and colour of this undiscovered landscape, the painters immortalised its shores on canvas, and in doing so advertised the savage beauty of the region. For neo-impressionists Paul Signac and Henri-Edmond Cross, the region provided a vision of utopia, while for Henri Matisse, the vivid colours of the area inspired him to adopt a new palette, and in doing so set modern art en route to abstraction. With visits to L'Estaque, St Tropez and Nice, Grant maps the progress of the region from cultural backwater to bohemian hotspot.

programme.title: Remembers...
programme.desc: Described by critics in 2016 as 'a powerhouse', 'jaw-dropping', 'hysterical' and 'the most shocking play on the London stage', David Ireland's Cyprus Avenue won huge international praise when it first opened and gave actor Stephen Rea the role of a lifetime in Eric, an Ulster Protestant who believes his recently born granddaughter is Gerry Adams. Here, writer David Ireland shares the story of how the play was born - from the first bizarre germ of idea that got him started, through to the casting and the challenges that came with his decision to make the leader of Sinn Fein so central to his narrative. David's recollections also include details of his approach to writing, his feelings on the filming of theatrical productions generally and his thoughts on the importance of catharsis and comedy when it comes to modern plays.

programme.title: Cyprus Avenue
programme.desc: David Ireland’s Cyprus Avenue is a multi-award-winning play and production starring Stephen Rea and directed by Vicky Featherstone. Originally co-produced at the Royal Court Theatre and Abbey Theatre, the critically acclaimed production went on tour to Belfast and New York. This adaptation mixes live capture of the performance from the stage of the Royal Court with location shooting in Belfast. Eric Miller is a Belfast loyalist. He experiences a psychotic episode and mistakes his five-week-old granddaughter for Gerry Adams. Generations of sectarian trauma convince him that his cultural heritage is under siege. He must act. A hard-hitting but in parts hilarious black comedy, Cyprus Avenue tells the story of a man struggling with the past and terrified of the future. It was awarded Best New Play at the Irish Times Theatre Awards and the James Tait Black Prize for Drama in 2017. Stephen Rea won Best Actor for his portrayal of Eric at the Irish Times Theatre Awards 2017. This recording, commissioned by The Space, creates a completely original adaptation.

programme.title: Discovering the Music of Antiquity
programme.desc: When a music score is uncovered deep within the storerooms of the Louvre, musical historians scramble to realise the potential of this piece of papyrus. The text's grammatical features give us a clue to the composer's identity: Carcinus, an author cited by Aristotle in his Rhetoric. His name is engraved on a wall in the Parthenon, and the story of his life offers an insight into the history of Greek musicians, who were revered like gods and welcomed across the Mediterranean to take part in competitions modelled on the Olympic Games. The discovery of the papyrus, more specifically an ancient version of the tragedy entitled Medea, throws open a new mission by researchers to hear the music sung through modern arrangement. But to listen to the Medea as it was heard by the Greeks 2,400 years ago, it still has to be played on period instruments. From the Greek cities of Anatolia to the Ptolemies’ Egypt, from the mythical site of Delphi to the discoveries made in Pompeii, relive this voyage along the Mediterranean coast, where archaeological excavations have unearthed instrument remains.

programme.title: Streets of Gold: Mumbai
programme.desc: It's the day before Holi, the Hindu festival that marks the beginning of Mumbai's scorching summer, a centuries-old celebration where the whole of India showers its streets and people in a rainbow of coloured dye. Young entrepreneur Sudipan Das is hoping plans to hold a ticketed festival for thousands of Mumbai's young revellers will be a success for what is traditionally a free event. Fashion Week is also underway in Mumbai's young and fashionable Bandra district, where we meet fashion models and flatmates, Shimona Nath and Chandani Purohit, both in their early twenties and both walking the runway. Shimona is already the face of India's most established make-up brand, Lakmé, and Chandani is working hard to realise her ambitions of making it as a model and in turn provide a better life for her family. Finally, we meet Yash Bhanage on opening day at Veronica's café in Bandra, in a city where a chapati and a cup of chai cost very little, the younger generation of Bandra think nothing of splashing out huge sums on a flat white and an artisan bagel.

programme.title: The Media Show
programme.desc: The right of reply has long been a cornerstone of journalism, giving those involved in a story the chance to respond before publication. But with politicians and public figures now using social media to publish their own version first, is this principle being undermined? Guto Harri, former Downing Street director of communications, Professor Karen Fowler-Watt from City St George's, University of London, and journalist Matt Shea assess how the practice is changing. As streaming services compete for attention, TV remotes usually now include buttons for platforms such as Netflix and YouTube, often paid for by the services themselves. UK broadcasters argue this disadvantages British platforms and have called for a dedicated 'British' button. Technology historian Edd Thomas and Professor Catherine Johnson from the University of Leeds explain why the remote has become such a significant battleground.

programme.title: AI Decoded
programme.desc: Has the AI industry finally recognised the dangers of the technology it is building? A researcher leaves one of the world's leading AI companies with a warning that the race to build ever more powerful systems could end in human extinction. Days later, the chief executive of the same company calls for the industry to slow down. This episode, AI Decoded examines the growing debate over AI safety, regulation and control. From fears that advanced systems could outpace human understanding to concerns over cyberattacks, biological threats and the challenge of containing increasingly powerful models, we ask whether the world's AI companies are moving too fast, and whether anyone can agree on how to slow down. The discussion also explores AI 'kill switches', international oversight, the role of governments, and whether rivalry between the United States and China makes meaningful cooperation impossible.

programme.desc: It's the day before Holi, the Hindu festival that marks the beginning of Mumbai's scorching summer, a centuries-old celebration where the whole of India showers its streets and people in a rainbow of coloured dye. Young entrepreneur Sudipan Das is hoping plans to hold a ticketed festival for thousands of Mumbai's young revellers will be a success for what is traditionally a free event. Fashion Week is also underway in Mumbai's young and fashionable Bandra district, where we meet fashion models and flatmates, Shimona Nath and Chandani Purohit, both in their early twenties and both walking the runway. Shimona is already the face of India's most established make-up brand, Lakmé, and Chandani is working hard to realise her ambitions of making it as a model and in turn provide a better life for her family. Finally, we meet Yash Bhanage on opening day at Veronica's café in Bandra, in a city where a chapati and a cup of chai cost very little, the younger generation of Bandra think nothing of splashing out huge sums on a flat white and an artisan bagel.

programme.title: AI Decoded
programme.desc: Has the AI industry finally recognised the dangers of the technology it is building? A researcher leaves one of the world's leading AI companies with a warning that the race to build ever more powerful systems could end in human extinction. Days later, the chief executive of the same company calls for the industry to slow down. This episode, AI Decoded examines the growing debate over AI safety, regulation and control. From fears that advanced systems could outpace human understanding to concerns over cyberattacks, biological threats and the challenge of containing increasingly powerful models, we ask whether the world's AI companies are moving too fast, and whether anyone can agree on how to slow down. The discussion also explores AI 'kill switches', international oversight, the role of governments, and whether rivalry between the United States and China makes meaningful cooperation impossible.

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: Natasha Raskin Sharp meets a man whose interest in antique lawn mowers over 50 years ago triggered a passion for the old, the rare and the extraordinary. At a garden centre in Bingley, a treasure trove of mowers, film projectors and miniature cars dangle above the plants. Hoping their buys are a cut above the rest are two teams of bargain hunters, scouring the aisles of a bustling antiques centre in West Yorkshire. In blue are engaged couple Luke and Megan shopping with their expert David Harper, and in red are brothers-in-law Sam and Kier, with Philip Serrell. A pair of blue German beer steins gets bar manager Luke all nostalgic, while a child’s wheelbarrow prompts Phil to reveal that he uses one at home to store his toilet rolls! Elsewhere, the blues select a penguin figurine as an option for Natasha’s challenge, and the reds go round in circles as they hesitate over their second purchase. At Caroline Hawley’s auction in Brough, Phil plans to keep his team in touch with his bonus buy, while David serves up a tasty treat for his duo.

programme.desc: The head nose of a family perfume company is found dead in suspicious circumstances. Most members of his family and staff have a motive to want him dead. Sister Boniface and the team investigate.

programme.title: Escape to the Country
programme.desc: With ambitions to start a cookery school in Shropshire, a couple from Hertfordshire get a helping hand from Nicki Chapman to spend £900,000 on a new home for their new life in the country. Getting to know the area and local producers, they all visit a small farm that supplies veggies to local restaurants and cafes.

programme.title: Garden Rescue
programme.desc: Charlie goes back to Pontefract to see one of the first gardens the team ever built. Originally, she and the Rich Brothers saw it under inches of snow, but it was soon turned into a gorgeous nature garden. Now, seven years later, Charlie discovers not only a riot of colour but an amazing new seating area that its owners have added. She also catches up with the couple in Stevenage who wanted a Chelsea Flower Show in their garden and ended up with something even better. And finally, seven years after the team left, there's another look at a garden inspired by an African landscape that is now even more like a piece of paradise.

programme.title: Antiques Road Trip
programme.desc: It’s the final run-out for experts Natasha Raskin Sharp and David Harper, and they're Yorkshire-bound in their bucking Bronco for one last blitz around the boutiques. Tash has a hankering for the eccentric, a cute but quirky coconut catches her eye, and could an unusual clock take flight at auction? Meanwhile, David charts a course towards some boating bounty, hoping it will steer him to auction success, and picks up a bit of philatelic history that could be first class. Taking a break from the shops, our pair step back in time, discovering the work that goes into keeping a collection of World War II military motors ticking over. David channels the spirit of Steve McQueen, and there's a surprise in store that has Tash and David ducking for cover! With their final auction looming, which one will win the week? Will those quirky curiosities soar in the saleroom or be cast adrift on troubled waters?

programme.title: The Travelling Auctioneers
programme.desc: A sci-fi fan wants to sell his rare and valuable collection of toys to fund a dream holiday for his family. David spent a considerable amount of time in hospital as a child, born with a condition affecting his muscles and joints. He found escape from the world around him in sci-fi, and the joy his Star Wars figures and toys gave him as a child continued as he grew older, and he expanded the collection. Four decades on, David's mobility has become limited, and he's become dependent on his wife, Sarah. Now, he wants to repay his family's sacrifices by selling his beloved collection to fund a dream holiday. He knows his Colchester home has boxes of treasured collectibles, but he's uncertain of their financial value. Auctioneer Izzie Balmer has just one day to work her way through an intergalactic world of sci-fi as she trawls through David's specialist collection. She hopes a surprise find in the loft could lead to a shock at auction. Meanwhile, JJ Chalmers finds the right tools in the blue van to fix an old tricycle, and he makes a musical sewing table sing once again. Will there be an out-of-this-world reaction to David's collection at auction?

programme.title: Celebrity MasterChef

The finalists must cook and present a faultless three-course meal for final judgement by Grace Dent and Giorgio Locatelli. It’s their last chance to prove they have what it takes, by showing true passion and creativity with their dishes. Who amongst this year’s finalists is the true cooking star and worthy of a place in the Celebrity MasterChef hall of fame? Only one can be crowned Celebrity MasterChef Champion 2026.

programme.title: Mary at 90: A Lifetime of Cooking
programme.desc: Sports broadcaster Gabby Logan joins Dame Mary in the kitchen to cook some of her standout time-saving recipes. Gabby asks Mary to share her own tales of being a working mum 50 years ago - the early days when Mary was one of the first TV cooks. Gabby is keen to cook, and she has come to the right place, because from the start of her career, the core of Mary’s focus has been helping busy working families with simple dishes for when time is short. Mary demonstrates a clever way to make mac and cheese with a freezer-friendly twist; her classic dill-cured gravadlax, prepped in moments and perfect to make ahead of time; horseradish beef cheeks, an updated version of a slow-cooked casserole classic; and Mary’s all-time favourite, a moreish and simple New York baked cheesecake.

programme.title: The Football Interview
programme.desc: The Football Interview sees the biggest names in sport and entertainment join host Kelly Somers for bold, in-depth conversations about the nation’s favourite sport. We explore mindset and motivation, reflect on defining moments and career highs, and discuss personal insights. It’s a chance to show an honest, human and sometimes surprising side to familiar faces. At the heart of this is Kelly Somers – one of the most trusted, versatile and authentic voices in sports broadcasting. Kelly brings a brand of warmth and relatability that resonates with both athletes and audiences. What sets her apart is her ability to dig deeper with a sensitive approach, creating a space where athletes feel comfortable being open, honest and at times vulnerable. Each episode sees Kelly draw out stories and insight from the player behind the name about the beautiful game, their origins and values, and a look-ahead to the future from a sporting and personal perspective. She takes her subjects on a journey – and takes the viewer with her.

It’s made of cast iron and features an unusual hook and handle, but what is it? Over in Wiltshire, auctioneer Tim Weeks is on the rostrum as he aims to deliver profits for both teams.

programme.desc: Jane, a retired archaeologist with a passion for history, has a small, terraced Victorian garden filled with treasures. After a 15-year career in archaeology and a prolonged battle with lung cancer, she now has the all-clear. To celebrate, Jane wants her garden made over. She would like either Charlie or Lee to design a relaxed, free-flowing garden with a seating area and a way to attract wildlife, and to combine flowers and vegetables together in a potager style. She’d also like the designers to recycle some of her archaeological finds in their designs. How will Lee and Charlie fare with a £6,000 budget?

programme.title: Countryfile
programme.desc: With the Bayeux Tapestry being displayed in Britain for the first time in almost a thousand years, Joe Crowley and Tom Heap are in East Sussex to discover what traces of this extraordinary story can still be found in the landscape today. Joe explores how the boats that carried the Norman army are still being built in East Sussex using traditional methods and investigates the region's flourishing vineyards, a feature of the landscape at the time of the conquest. Tom meets a farmer rearing descendants of the native long-horned red cattle depicted in the tapestry and walks the battlefield from both Norman and Saxon perspectives, examining how the terrain shaped the course of the conflict.

programme.title: Antiques Roadshow
programme.desc: The roadshow visits Valentines Mansion in Ilford, east London. Treasures include an aquamarine art deco brooch, a Tongan war club and a rare and valuable Faberge clock.

programme.title: The Split Up
programme.desc: Aria Kishan, a leading divorce lawyer for Manchester’s elite, is poised to take the reins from her father, Dhruv, at Kishan Law, the family firm he founded after he moved to the UK from India years ago. She has big aspirations for the company, including moving away from their current premises and expanding at a new upmarket location. But Dhruv wonders if she can take on the responsibility of Kishan Law alone. Aria’s wedding preparations to steady long-term partner Neal have been paused following the tragic death of her mother, Raina, six months ago. Raina was sick, and Aria moved back in with Dhruv to help care for her and has stayed since to make sure her dad was managing. However, her family have decided Aria can’t put her life on hold any longer and decide to help by planning a surprise engagement party for her and Neal. This coincides with Luke, a secret former flame of Aria’s, arriving at the firm, and all of her well-formed plans for her future start to spiral out of control.

programme.desc: Sports mockumentary about GB Paralympian Darren Silverstone, who stole the hearts of a nation before his infamous chokey-o in Tokyo. For the first time, he tells his story - and starts his glorious comeback. In Tokyo 2020, Darren Silverstone was the Paras GB poster boy. (He was on yoghurts, too.) He cruised to the final and charmed the nation along the way with his signature dance move, the dazzle. But as he took that final bend ready to take gold, Silverstone lost his head and celebrated too soon - and in the process, became a national figure of fun. His subsequent journey in the public eye brought approval and consternation in equal measure: from those unforgettably self-deprecating betting adverts to his turn on The Masked Singer as Breadbin. Darren’s best friend and pilot rider in Tokyo, little Paul Potter, was never seen again in the public eye. The two haven’t spoken since. And now, Silverstone’s back. Ready to take to the tandem at Paris 2024. But is he ready? Who will he be riding with? This is I Am Darren.

programme.title: Back to the Future Part II
programme.desc: Marty and Doc once again climb into the DeLorean and travel back to the future in an attempt to put 1985, and their lives, back to normal.

programme.title: Death in Paradise
programme.desc: Selwyn’s return to Saint Marie is disrupted by a suspicious death at Government House, where a man has fallen from the roof. It looks like a suicide, but DI Mervin Wilson suspects foul play. However, no-one was on the roof with the victim when he fell, and he had locked the roof door behind him. So, if this man was pushed, how did it happen? Meanwhile, Mervin is anxious to finally meet his half-brother Solomon, the other son of the mother Mervin never knew. Granted, the pair have never met before, but family’s family! Surely, they'll get on like a house on fire?

programme.title: Cunk on...
programme.desc: Philomena Cunk visits the allegedly beautiful city of Florence to explore the Renaissance and interrogates experts and historians about the revolutions that went on to shape the modern world, including the American War of Independence and, to a lesser extent, the French Revolution.

programme.title: Cunk on...
programme.desc: Cunk continues her ambitious march across the face of mankind into an age of industry and science. With the help of historians, she explains the scientific breakthroughs of Marie Curie and Albert Einstein. She demonstrates the inventions that changed the world and covers how the American Civil War, World War I and World War II taught humanity how to use its new grasp of technology to shoot, blow up and irradiate itself in huge numbers.

programme.title: Cunk on...
programme.desc: In the final episode of her epic journey across history, Philomena Cunk takes us from 1945 to the present day. She travels the world and meets top experts to examine the Cold War, the space race, globalisation and social media. The world's recent history is one of polarisation and division as humanity divided itself down the middle – communism v capitalism, Apple v Microsoft, Beatles v Stones. Is humanity doomed to repeat the mistakes of history? Cunk does her best to find out.

programme.title: Ideal
programme.desc: Sitcom about a small-time dope dealer. Moz plots to win back Jenny, but when he discovers she has joined the police force, his plans are thrown into disarray.

programme.title: Ideal
programme.desc: Sitcom about a small-time dope dealer. A penniless Moz calls in his debts. However, his mates seem reluctant to pay him back. Jess falls under the spell of Cartoon Head.

programme.title: Ideal
programme.desc: Moz and Nicki start running rival hash dealing businesses, but a price war soon kicks off with each attempting to undercut the other. Across the landing, Brian and Carmel have opened a brothel.

programme.title: Ideal
programme.desc: Mistakenly believing Moz to be an avant-garde artist, Tilly arranges an exhibition for him. Jess and Cartoon Head experiment with ketamine and find themselves way out of their depth.

programme.title: Ideal

programme.title: My Mate's a Bad Date
programme.desc: Twenty-five-year-old Mancunian Tyler is a self-confessed serial dater who treats dating like a sport and goes on five or six dates a week. She’s rude and sarcastic, rambles on about herself, gets bored easily and doesn’t stay focused on her dates. Best mate Yazmine is sick of hearing about Tyler’s dating disasters. Tyler needs help, so Yazmine calls on Gen Z’s most trusted sex and relationships expert, Oloni, to kick-start an intervention. Oloni pulls Tyler up on her catastrophic dating habits and delivers some tough truths as she and Tyler watch frank video feedback from friends and exes to prove to Tyler that there needs to be a change. Oloni has her job cut out with this one and sets Tyler up on three challenge dates as she and Yazmine watch on. Tyler insists her ideal date is the male version of herself, but will the male ‘Tyler’ be the perfect match for this feisty female?

programme.title: My Mate's a Bad Date
programme.desc: Cardiff-based hopeless romantic Lewis just can’t help hearing wedding bells and talking through future life plans on date one, but that’s not the only obstacle to him getting a second date. If he’s not ranting about his exes, he’s zoning out mid-conversation, leaving his dates lost for words and never calling them again. Tired of listening to yet another of his first-date failures, Lewis’s best mate Megan thinks it’s time for an intervention, so she enlists the help one of Gen Z’s sassiest sex and relationships experts, Oloni, to drop some hard home truths on 20-year-old Lewis to try to end the bad habits that send his dates running for the hills. Oloni gives Lewis a reality check as his friends and exes tell it how it is via video feedback, explaining where it’s all going wrong. Oloni and Megan watch on as Lewis goes on a series of first dates that will challenge him to rethink his dating behaviour and become a better dater. Can Lewis ditch the wedding planning, stop raking up stories about his exes and focus on the conversation long enough to prove he can be a good date?

programme.title: BBC New Comedy Awards
programme.desc: The BBC’s big comedy talent search, the New Comedy Awards, is scouring the country to uncover the hottest new stand-ups. We head to London and the historic Alexandra Palace, home of the BBC’s first broadcast. Five comics will battle it out to book their place in this year’s grand final showdown, where one will be crowned the BBC New Comedian of 2025. Hosting the comedy extravaganza is comedian, actor, presenter and writer Sara Pascoe. Joining her are the three judges, two of whom are former New Comedy Awards finalists, stand-up comics Catherine Bohart and Michael Odewale, plus head judge, Fatiha El-Ghorri. Blank Peng, Fab Goualin, Sharifa Butterfly, Sydney May and Evaldas Karosas each perform their set before the judges decide who will go through to the Grand Final in November. There can only be one winner, so who will it be? This is just one of six heats taking place across the UK - Belfast, Glasgow, Bristol, Newcastle and Birmingham all play host to these comedy showdowns.

programme.title: Mrs Brown's Boys
programme.desc: Dermot and Maria's wedding is just days away and tensions are running high in the Brown household. The groom is getting cold feet. His best man Buster can't find anything good to say about Dermot in his speech. To cap it all Agnes Brown is mystified as to why her daughter Cathy has given her a book on homosexuality. Is she trying to tell her mother that one of the family is gay? When Dermot's pre-marriage nerves get the better of him, he does what he always does when stressed. He locks himself in the cupboard. Father Quinn is bemused to have to give Maria and Dermot their pre-marriage talk in slightly unusual circumstances - with the mother of the groom in attendance and the groom in the cupboard. If Dermot won't reappear for the priest, how on earth is Agnes going to persuade him to come out in time for his wedding? Meanwhile, Agnes Brown goes on a hunt for the homosexual in the family. Eventually she realises who it is. With help from Cathy and a greetings card, Agnes reassures them, and herself, as only she can.

programme.title: Mrs Brown's Boys
programme.desc: Agnes Brown thinks everyone has gone mad. Father Quinn is losing his faith as fast as he loses parishioners. Newlyweds Dermot and Maria will not stop fighting. And Grandad has decided that he would like to witness his own funeral. He is keen to hear all the nice things people will say about him at his funeral while he is still alive to enjoy them. Maria tells Mrs Brown why she and Dermot have been arguing so much. She thinks that they should move out of the Brown household, but Dermot is resisting. He is also scheming with Buster to make some quick cash so that he can afford a first home for him and Maria. The Browns decide to make Grandad happy by faking his funeral, but their plans start to go awry when Mrs Brown mistakes two Mormons for the men who are supposed to be delivering Grandad's coffin. In the event, Grandad is horrified to find that no-one has a kind word to say about him after all, and the mourners get a shock when the corpse comes back to life. Only a quick-thinking Mrs Brown can save the day.

programme.desc: Sam and Jay face new pressures threatening their control of Woodstone, forcing them to tackle unexpected challenges. A ghost who's been gone returns, stirring up emotions that complicate existing relationships.

programme.title: The Edge
programme.desc: Gabby Logan takes charge of the quiz where contestants need brainpower and ball skills to win big. Who will be the high roller and who will push themselves over The Edge?

programme.title: Unbeatable
programme.desc: Jason Manford hosts the quiz where it's not just about finding the right answer, it's finding the best answer that counts. Four contestants go head-to-head throughout the game, but only one will make it through to the final and win thousands of pounds if they prove themself Unbeatable.

programme.title: Great British Railway Journeys
programme.desc: Armed with his interwar copy of Bradshaw’s Guide to the Railways, Michael reaches the Kent seaside resort of Herne Bay, where he learns about a pioneering aviatrix who began her working life as a typist in Hull but whose epic achievements made her an international celebrity. Michael takes the train five miles west along the coast before heading offshore into the entrance to the Thames Estuary. He is amazed by seven enormous steel sea forts, which loom out of the water 90 feet above the seabed. The engineering involved in constructing these impressive structures is awe-inspiring, as is their role in protecting the nation from enemy bombing during the Second World War. In the seaside town of Whitstable, Michael tucks into its famous staple, oysters. He then crosses the North Downs to Lenham, from which he visits Leeds Castle, the 'loveliest castle in the world' and home between the wars to the visionary Lady Olive Bailey.

programme.title: Eva Longoria: Searching for Mexico
programme.desc: Eva takes a tour of her adopted hometown in the heart of the country. She devours a freshly baked concha at her favourite neighbourhood bakery and travels by boat down a network of Aztec canals to an ancient floating vegetable garden, before meeting food writer Gabriela Renteria for an unforgettable tour of the city’s famous tacos.

programme.title: Wild China
programme.desc: China's heartland is the centre of a 5,000-year-old civilization and is home to the giant panda, the golden snub-nosed monkey and the golden takin. China faces environmental problems, but the relationship the Chinese have with their environment is deep and extraordinary. We will understand what this means for the future of China.

programme.title: Flog It!
programme.desc: Paul Martin presents from Muncaster Castle in Cumbria, where hundreds of people turn up with collectibles and treasures they want to take to auction. Antiques experts Adam Partridge and Caroline Hawley uncover a few gems including a silver candlestick and some Coalbrookedale plates, and Paul delves into the Lake District's bobbin industry.

programme.title: Richard Osman's House of Games
programme.desc: Every day this week, celebrity contestants Larry Dean, Kirsty Gallagher, Sam Quek and Lemn Sissay take on a series of quiz rounds selected by the host, quiz legend Richard Osman. A daily winner is declared following a quick-fire round at the end of each show, and the scores are tallied across the week, resulting in an overall champion being crowned on Friday. Will the winning stars opt for the much-coveted House of Games suitcase, or will they be tempted with the House of Games bee hotel?

programme.title: Clive Myrie’s Caribbean Adventure
programme.desc: Clive heads for the east coast of Barbados to check out the world’s oldest rum distillery. He explores the sugar cane fields and the factory floor before he gets the chance to have a sip of the golden produce. He puts a shift in with the hens on an organic family farm that stretches out for over 100 acres, tests out his flexibility alongside British expats with some cliff-top yoga and finally meets a young Bajan spoken word poet at the Builders of Barbados wall.

programme.title: Newsnight
programme.desc: Insights and global interviews on the crucial news stories of the day. With Matt Chorley.

programme.title: Beechgrove Garden
programme.desc: Dealing with the changing seasons, and Scotland’s weather, is a theme running through Beechgrove Garden’s horticultural advice. Brian Cunningham looks at which trees you can plant that will cope with wet conditions, and he also looks at what plants you should be bringing indoors for protection as the nights get colder. Lizzie Schofield demonstrates how to take autumn seeds and cultivate for spring seedlings. Carole Baxter is back with another of her visits to a great Scottish garden; this time, she visits a plot in Wester Ross.

programme.title: Gardeners' World
programme.desc: In a special programme exploring the enduring value of allotment life, Frances Tophill heads to Exmouth in Devon, where thriving plots and passionate growers are at the heart of a vibrant community. At a time when more people want to know where their food comes from and enjoy the unbeatable taste of home-grown produce, Frances discovers why these much-loved spaces matter more than ever. Joe Swift heads to Manchester to offer advice to newbie allotmenteer De-Graft Mensah, who, when not presenting Newsround, can’t get enough of growing his own food. There’s a determined plot holder in Scarborough who refuses to let a pigeon-led brassica massacre get the better of her. And in Bradford, two allotment holders share how, for them, a love of growing has forged an unlikely friendship that bridges generations. And in a dramatic finale, actors Zoë Henry and Jeff Hordley - better known as Rhona Goskirk and Cain Dingle from Emmerdale - share the real-life soap opera behind their much-loved allotment and dig the dirt on who really does most of the work.

programme.title: Michael Portillo's 200 Years of the Railways
programme.desc: Railway enthusiast Michael Portillo follows the route of the pioneering Stockton and Darlington Railway in north east England - the world’s first public railway to carry fee-paying passengers using steam locomotives. He learns how the Stockton and Darlington proved that railways could work - sparking a transport revolution across Britain and beyond. He visits key locations in the story of this pioneering railway, including the town of Shildon, from where the train hauled by Locomotion No.1 set off in 1825; Bishop Auckland, where he joins thousands at a spectacular outdoor show to launch the 200th anniversary and drives a replica of the original train; and the Tyne and Wear Metro, where he discovers a new fleet transforming travel in north east England.

programme.title: The Devil’s Confession: The Lost Eichmann Tapes
programme.desc: Escaping from postwar Europe, Nazi criminal Adolf Eichmann establishes a new life in Argentina, where he meets fellow Nazi Willem Sassen. Together, they record a comprehensive account of his career. The tapes disappear when Eichmann is captured and taken to stand trial in Jerusalem, but excerpts of his interview surface in Life Magazine, and Israeli prosecutor Gideon Hausner is determined to use Eichmann’s recorded confession as evidence during the trial.

programme.title: Starve Acre
programme.desc: In the rural England of the 1970s, Richard and Julie's seemingly idyllic family life is thrown into turmoil when their son starts acting out of character. At Starve Acre, their remote family home, archaeologist Richard buries himself in exploring a folkloric myth that the ancient oak tree on their land is imbued with phenomenal powers. While Julie turns to the local community to find some kind of peace, Richard obsessively digs deeper.

programme.title: Panorama
programme.desc: It’s a sex abuse scandal that has gripped the world. But despite all the headlines and stories, important questions remain unanswered about Jeffrey Epstein. How did he become so powerful? How did he befriend so many important people? And where did the money come from that allowed him to abuse hundreds of girls and young women? Panorama follows the crooked money trail to show how Epstein conned and ingratiated his way into the lives of the super-rich and then used their money to fund his global sex trafficking operation.

programme.title: The Big Deal with Steph McGovern
programme.desc: Four pairs of aspiring art dealers remain to compete in the semi-final, and all of them have their eyes on the ultimate prize of £50,000 worth of British art. To take them one step closer, host Steph and series mentor Cordelia de Freitas welcome them onboard the luxurious Queen Anne cruise ship, where they’ll spend three days at sea, working to a specific brief and stepping into the world of art curation. Joined by guest mentors and curators Wilhelm Finger and Melita Skamnaki, the pairs are once again split into teams before being tasked with curating a collection of art fit for the ship’s newest cabaret bar. One team secures a lucrative deal, while one pair faces elimination.

programme.title: Beechgrove Garden
programme.desc: Dealing with the changing seasons, and Scotland’s weather, is a theme running through Beechgrove Garden’s horticultural advice. Brian Cunningham looks at which trees you can plant that will cope with wet conditions, and he also looks at what plants you should be bringing indoors for protection as the nights get colder. Lizzie Schofield demonstrates how to take autumn seeds and cultivate for spring seedlings. Carole Baxter is back with another of her visits to a great Scottish garden; this time, she visits a plot in Wester Ross.

programme.title: The Great British Sewing Bee
programme.desc: It’s the grand finale, and the remaining candidates are ready to compete for the coveted title of Britain’s best amateur sewer. The judges, Patrick Grant and Esme Young, set three challenges inspired to test their skills for one final time. First up, the sewers get gala ready with a cummerbund and bow tie. Next, it’s time for the transformation challenge, where the sewers take gala tableware and turn it into an outfit for the perfect day-after hangout, the beach club. Finally, inspired by the Met Gala in New York, the sewers must create outfits on the theme of metamorphosis as if they had an invite to the Sewing Bee gala. Three finalists, three challenges, but only one contestant will be crowned the twelfth champion of The Great British Sewing Bee.

programme.title: Race Against the Tide
programme.desc: The tide waits for no-one – and neither does the pressure! Our final four teams of sandy dreamers hit the Scottish shores of St Andrews for their toughest challenge yet: Sky’s the Limit. Their brief is to build big, with towering sculptures that defy gravity and the incoming waves. With drama, collapses and plenty of sand-fuelled fun as the clock ticks down from yellow flag to red, who will soar into the final, and who will crumble under the weight of their own ambition?

programme.title: Women's Super League
programme.desc: London City Lionesses meet local rivals Charlton Athletic in the Women's Super League.

programme.title: West Side Story
programme.desc: Classic Broadway musical. The tensions between rival gangs the Jets, whose members include 'white' Americans, and a Puerto Rican gang, the Sharks, reach boiling point in a hot New York summer. At a neighbourhood dance, Tony, the co-founder of the Jets, meets Maria, the sister of Bernardo, the leader of the Sharks. Their romance is thwarted by the gang rivalries.

programme.title: Rugby League: Super League
programme.desc: Action from the elimination play-offs as Warrington face Hull KR.

programme.title: Golf: PGA Championship
programme.desc: Action from day 3 at Wentworth as a world-class field contest the flagship event on the DP World Tour. Two-time winner Alex Noren starts as defending champion following a dramatic play-off victory in the 2025 event. Other previous winners include Rory McIlroy, Luke Donald, Seve Ballesteros and Nick Faldo.

programme.title: Natural World
programme.desc: Members of the weasel family are often portrayed as the villains of the natural world, but do they deserve this reputation? By following the adventures of a tiny orphaned weasel named Twiz, this film reveals the true nature of these pocket-sized predators, which relative to their size have a bite more powerful than a tiger’s. In Yorkshire, a unique garden rigged with over 50 cameras gives a rare insight into the dramatic life of a mother stoat as she tries to raise her first family. And new science uncovers the problem-solving abilities of the honey badger, the secrets behind the ferret’s legendary flexibility, and the remarkable sense of smell of the wolverine. Together, using their extraordinary skills, this feisty and fearless family have conquered the planet.

programme.title: Glastonbury
programme.desc: From the Glastonbury Festival, the complete set by the undisputed queen of country music Dolly Parton from the Pyramid Stage in the now-traditional legends spot on Sunday afternoon. As the Somerset sunshine shone, and in front of one of the biggest and most enthusiastic crowds that the Pyramid Stage has ever seen, Dolly performed a rousing and crowd-pleasing set including self-penned classics such as Jolene, Coat of Many Colours, 9 to 5, Islands in the Stream and I Will Always Love You. A legendary moment that the Glastonbury crowd and hopefully Dolly Parton will never forget.

programme.title: Sisters in Country: Dolly, Linda and Emmylou
programme.desc: How Dolly Parton, Linda Ronstadt and Emmylou Harris's careers took off in the 1970s with distinct takes on country, and how they ended up uniting as close harmony singers on Trio.

programme.title: Dolly Parton at the BBC
programme.desc: Dolly Parton is one of the biggest and best-loved music stars on the planet. Here, we celebrate all things Dolly with a look back at some of her greatest performances on the BBC, incorporating all her biggest hits and finest moments. From Jolene and 9 to 5, to Islands in the Stream and Here You Come Again, this collection showcases the enduring songwriting talents and the sense of humour that first made her name back in the 1970s.

programme.title: Green Man Festival
programme.desc: Aleighcia Scott and Katie Owen present highlights from Green Man Festival 2026, the independent, sold-out festival in the Bannau Brycheiniog. Featuring live performances from Wolf Alice, The Beta Band, The Tubs, Panic Shack, Mwsog and Pigeon, shot with a warm, filmic style that captures the music alongside the atmosphere, rituals and landscape that make Green Man distinctive.

programme.title: T20 Cricket
programme.desc: Highlights of the third game of the T20 series between England and Sri Lanka.

programme.title: Kidnapped
programme.desc: Powerful drama based on the true story of the Catholic Church's kidnap of a young Jewish boy. Italy, 1858. Following Pope Pius IX’s orders, soldiers burst into the Mortara family’s Bologna home to forcibly remove their six-year-old son, Edgardo. They have heard from the Jewish family’s maid that she had secretly baptised him as a sickly infant for fear that he would die a Jew and his soul would remain in limbo. Under the Church’s doctrine, the boy is no longer permitted to live with his non-Catholic family and is taken to be raised by the Church itself. The distraught Mortara family try desperately to get Edgardo back, and the scandal soon makes its way across the country and Europe at large. As they embark on an international campaign to have their son returned, they find themselves at the epicentre of a wider historical battle between the forces of Catholic authoritarianism and the political awakening taking place across Italy and throughout Europe. In Italian with English subtitles

programme.title: This is BBC Two
programme.desc: Highlights of programmes on BBC Two.

programme.title: Countryfile
programme.desc: Joe Crowley, Datshiane Navanayagam and Adam Henson head to Westacre Estate in Norfolk to discover how a historic rural estate is adapting to survive in the modern world. At a financially critical time of year, Datshiane looks at one of the estate's most valuable yet vulnerable crops, blueberries, and meets the estate owner to find out how traditional estates are diversifying and evolving to secure their future. Joe joins the conservation team as they work to restore an important area of wet woodland, boosting biodiversity and creating habitats for wildlife. He also visits a tenant brewery and lends a hand to craft a local ale. Meanwhile, Adam meets the estate's farm manager, who is looking at ways to help run the land in a more cost-effective way through collaboration between livestock and arable farming.

programme.title: Breakfast
programme.desc: The latest news, sport, business and weather from the BBC's Breakfast team.

programme.title: Weatherman Walking
programme.desc: Derek explores what lies beneath his feet when he revisits the Great Orme, the Offa’s Dyke Path and the last surviving cast iron footbridge in Merthyr Tydfil.

programme.title: Landward
programme.desc: The Landward team return for the autumn. Dougie is in the Cairngorms to find out how wildlife and precious habitats have been impacted by the summer’s devastating wildfire. Anne reports from the ongoing scene of the fire to see the collective effort to put it out. Shahbaz is in Tayside meeting the scientists using technology to select the crops of the future, and Cammy learns the ropes as he takes part in a clifftop rescue with the coastguard.

programme.title: Saturday Kitchen Best Bites
programme.desc: Matt Tebbutt delivers a tasting menu from favourite Saturday Kitchen chefs. Shivi Ramoutar prepares her green seasoning chicken with coconut rice, peas and a splash of hot pepper sauce. Yotam Ottolenghi dishes up fillets of halibut in a spicy tomato sauce with a tahini dressing and a side of mint and feta-baked rice. Philip Khoury whips up his two-ingredient chocolate mousse served with an abundance of toppings, including chocolate curls, candied pistachios and pistachio praline. Gemma Ogston creates a rainbow curry and spiced apple chutney, and Helen McGinn celebrates an iconic cocktail, the negroni, with a few twists on the classic recipe. Finally, either Harry Judd or his mum Emma face their food heaven. Meanwhile, Rick Stein goes fishing for langoustines in the Scottish Highlands, and the Hairy Bikers explore the melting pot of flavours in Marseilles.

programme.title: Lorraine Pascale: How to Be a Better Cook
programme.desc: With plenty of deceptively easy recipes and fantastic tips, Lorraine Pascale shows people with no kitchen confidence how to pull off an impressive meal for friends and family. Neil Forster is an impatient cook who reaches for the takeaway menu rather than making food from scratch. Lorraine shows him recipes including asparagus and cream cheese puff pastry tarts, a quick way to do roast chicken and an irresistible summer fruits pudding with a neat shortcut.

programme.title: Nigel and Adam's Farm Kitchen
programme.desc: Nigel Slater and Adam Henson join forces to sow, grow, rear and cook Britain's favourite foods, from a working farm in the Cotswolds. Revealing the top 50 fresh foods on the UK's supermarket shopping lists, Nigel and Adam show how we can get the most flavour, value and variety from them all. The duo look at how our busy lifestyles have meant Britain has lost touch with where our food comes from and the best ways to cook it. With the rise of convenience foods meaning a decline in traditional cooking, can Nigel bring the art of cooking back to Britain? Nigel cooks up our favourite ready meal, lasagne, and tries to match the price of the off-the-shelf version of this popular dish. Adam, meanwhile, sets his own challenge to grow durum wheat, used to make pasta, on the Cotswolds farm. This episode also explores the UK's favourite red meat - beef - and the journey it takes from farm to fork, before Nigel inspires us to get around the table again by cooking a supersized Sunday roast for his guests on the farm.

programme.title: Natural World
programme.desc: A real-life drama about a family of chimps trapped in a lost world. They live in a deep and ancient forested gorge that runs though the African savannah. For 15 years, it has been cut off from the rest of the jungle, leaving the chimps imprisoned. The family face a daily life-or-death dilemma: whether to leave the safety of the gorge and venture into the predator-ridden savannah to find food, or face hunger. There's now only 20 of them left, and as Brutus the alpha male loses his grip, can the family hold it together, or is time running out for the Kyambura chimps?

programme.title: The Big Deal with Steph McGovern
programme.desc: It’s the grand finale, and for the three pairs of aspiring art dealers who have made it through, the ultimate prize of £50,000 of British art is almost within touching distance. Rejoining Steph and series mentor Cordelia de Freitas is guest expert Matt Carey-Williams. The remaining pairs are tested on everything they’ve learnt so far as they’re thrown into the biggest event in the UK art calendar – Frieze Week. For seven days, London becomes the centre of the art universe. After competing to sell art against established art dealers and gallerists for the first time at one of the week's most popular art fairs, one pair is eliminated, and the final two pairs must pitch a six-figure sculpture to a group of industry insiders at the prestigious Frieze sculpture park.

programme.title: Cycling: World Road Championships
programme.desc: Jill Douglas presents live coverage of the UCI Road World Championships women’s time trial – being held for the second time in Montreal, Canada. Switzerland’s Marlon Reusser is looking to retain the title she won in Rwanda last year, but Great Britain’s promising youngster and multiple junior title winner Zoe Backstedt is aiming for her first senior World Championship podium. Commentary comes from Simon Brotherton, Chris Boardman and Hayley Simmonds.

programme.title: Flog It!
programme.desc: Paul Martin and the team are in the picturesque village of Saltaire, West Yorkshire. It is a world heritage site, so with a historic pedigree like that, expectations are running high with experts David Barby and Michael Baggott. David finds six tasty sandwich markers, but Michael digs out a real treasure - a 400-year-old Laurel gold coin circa 1603 to 1625. Paul also visits Temple Newsam, a 17th-century house being restored to its former glory by a dedicated and skilled team.

programme.title: Celebrity Antiques Road Trip
programme.desc: We've taken three soap stars from the road trip archives to see who will clean up at auction. Emmerdale actress Hayley Tamaddon is up against Corrie's Will Mellor and former Queen Vic landlord and all-round geezer Danny Dyer from EastEnders. Ably assisting our soap opera icons are antiques experts and superfans Raj Bisram, Paul Laidlaw and Natasha Raskin Sharp, guiding our stars to all manner of antique items. Will gets to grips with a rather unusual truncheon, Danny has his eye on an intriguing optical instrument, and Hayley takes a punt on some carousel horses. Bring on the drama!

programme.title: Golf: PGA Championship
programme.desc: Action from the final day at Wentworth as a world class field contest the flagship event on the DP World Tour. The winner at the iconic Surrey venue adds their name to an illustrious list of previous champions, including Rory McIlroy, Luke Donald, Seve Ballesteros and Nick Faldo. Two-time winner Alex Noren defends the title he won in 2025 after a dramatic play-off victory.

programme.title: Secrets of the Bayeux Tapestry: Inside the Museum
programme.desc: The Bayeux Tapestry is one of the treasures of the medieval world. Across 70 metres of exquisitely embroidered scenes, it tells the story of one of the most seismic events in British history – the Norman Invasion of 1066. For the last 950 years, this crucial part of Britain's national story has remained on the other side of the English Channel, in Bayeux, Normandy, but now it’s coming back to the UK. A stellar cast of historians and experts follow the painstaking efforts to bring this priceless work of art back to the UK, where experts believe it was made, for a once-in-a-millennium exhibition at the British Museum.

programme.title: Pilgrimage
programme.desc: Seven celebrities of differing faiths and beliefs experience an emotional journey on a pilgrimage in north Wales, a route linked by churches dedicated to early Celtic Christian saints. Immersing themselves on this spiritual journey are wildlife presenter Michaela Strachan, who places her faith in the natural world; Spencer Matthews, a former Made in Chelsea reality star who was christened in the Church of England but is still searching for answers to life’s big questions; Sonali Shah, a journalist and TV presenter who grew up in a Jain family; comedian Eshaan Akbar, a lapsed Muslim; Amanda Lovett, a practising Catholic who was catapulted into the public eye in the first series of Traitors; actor Tom Rosenthal of Friday Night Dinner fame, who is areligious; and TV personality and former model Christine McGuinness, who is spiritual but doesn’t practise one particular faith. Travelling on foot and by bus, the seven pilgrims begin their adventure at Flint Castle on the bank of the Dee Estuary and follow the coastal path to Greenfield Valley, the official start of the 220km Pilgrim’s Way.

programme.title: Wilderness with Simon Reeve
programme.desc: Simon Reeve ventures deep into one of the most remote and biologically rich regions on Earth, the rainforests of Papua New Guinea, in search of one of the rarest creatures on the planet - the tenkile tree kangaroo. Covering just a tiny fraction of the planet’s land surface, tropical rainforests hold more than half of the world’s plant and animal species – and few places rival New Guinea for sheer diversity. The island is home to vast wilderness areas that remain little known to science, a lost world with countless species still undiscovered.

programme.title: Slumdog Millionaire
programme.desc: An orphan from the slums of Mumbai makes it all the way to the final question of Who Wants to Be a Millionaire. The police think he must be cheating, but Jamal's whole life has led to this moment.

programme.title: Saving Lives at Sea
programme.desc: When a kayaker calls a friend to say she’s in trouble out at sea, the line suddenly goes dead; the Happisburgh lifeboat crew finally find her over a mile off shore, face down and unresponsive. In St Helier, the capital of Jersey, a family have had to abandon their grounded yacht, leaving four young children in a life raft. On the north Yorkshire coast, the Withernsea crew respond to a 999 call from a young man cut off on some notoriously unstable cliffs. And in Littlehampton, West Sussex, a mayday call comes in from a dive boat that has lost engine power - leaving two of its divers drifting away.

programme.title: Crossing
programme.desc: Retired Georgian teacher Lia is on a mission to find her long-lost niece, a trans woman called Tekla, who is rumoured to have moved to Istanbul and whom Lia promised her dying sister she would bring home. Lia finds an unlikely companion in Achi, the hapless young son of one of her former pupils, who insists he has important information about Lia's niece's whereabouts and who is itching to leave home. Together, Lia and Achi set out on their journey, crossing the border into Turkey and venturing into the big city in search of missing Tekla. In Georgian, Turkish and English.

programme.title: Duck and Frog
programme.desc: Duck must pick up leaves from the park, but Frog's arrival makes it seem impossible. That is, until Frog comes up with a clever solution - using springs from Duck’s beloved chair!

programme.desc: When Duck and Frog get a job in a restaurant kitchen, Frog accidentally makes the soup incredibly spicy. He wants to serve it to a celebrity chef, but Duck wants to stop him!

programme.title: Shark Bites
programme.desc: Steve Backshall looks at our very own gentle giant - the basking shark. This is a huge shark that we have right here in the UK, and for such a sizeable shark, it has a somewhat surprising diet. It visits our coastal waters every spring and summer, and Steve heads to his shark lab to reveal why.

programme.title: Bitesize Daily: 5-7 Year Olds
programme.desc: Learn how to design butterflies, sculpt them and choose colours.

programme.title: Horrible Histories
programme.desc: Historical sketch show based on the successful books. Queen Victoria learns that her British comforts are not very British, a Viking warrior won't stop talking in rhyme, and on 'Axe Factor', the contestants try to become executioners.

programme.title: Horrible Science
programme.desc: Big Brain has a chemical catastrophe, Sir Isaac Newton rides a coaster again, with shocking results, Loofah is after a murderer, and Dr Henry VIII is on call!

programme.title: Operation Ouch!
programme.desc: The doctors explain how we breathe by inflating a real pig's lung, and Xand finds out all about the biological changes that happen when you hold your breath. Dr Chris gets icky and picky as he takes a very close look at the job that snot, bogies and mucus do in our bodies. And there's no need to be scared of scars as we find out how your skin heals itself after an injury. Meanwhile, over in accident and emergency, one patient is rushed in with a worrying eye injury after a dangerous accident with a pellet gun, and the trauma team is on standby as another comes into hospital with a potentially serious head injury.

programme.title: Ricky Wilson's Art Jam
programme.desc: Radio 1 DJ Nick ‘Grimmy’ Grimshaw visits the Art Jam studio to show Ricky three items that mean the world to him - a colourful Keith Haring print, a picture of a Paris bridge wrapped in gold fabric and a special Damien Hirst album cover. While chatting to Ricky, Nick shares amazing stories about being a DJ, the celebrities he has met, his lifelong love of art and his two beloved dogs.

programme.title: Africa
programme.desc: David Attenborough takes a breathtaking journey through the vast and diverse continent of Africa as it has never been seen before. In Africa's ancient south west corner, two extraordinary deserts sit side by side. Water is in short supply, yet these deserts are somehow full of life because the creatures that live here have turned the rules of survival on their head. This film celebrates nature's ingenuity, no matter how tough it gets. In the Kalahari scrublands, clever meerkats are outsmarted by a wily bird, solitary and belligerent black rhinos get together to party and giant insects stalk huge flocks of birds. Rain almost never falls in the Namib - instead it must make do with vaporous, vanishing fog. The creatures in this, the world's oldest desert, have gone to the extremes, as spiders wheel to escape and a desert giraffe fights to defend his scant resources in the greatest giraffe battle ever filmed.

programme.title: Game on Grandparents
programme.desc: Skilled kid gamers coach their novice grandparents to compete in an epic esports battle in the hope of becoming the GOAT of Game on Grandparents! Girls and boys who dream of playing at an eSports tournament are about to get the chance, but there is a twist - they won't be playing themselves but instead have to train their gran or grandad! While their grandparents are busy practising, the children have to take on their roles about the house, from washing up or walking the dog, to entertaining grandma’s friends for the afternoon – what could possibly go wrong?!

programme.title: Andy and the Band
programme.desc: Attempting to become young again, Whiff accidentally turns the Odd Socks into babies! With Whiff as their babysitter, how will the baby-faced band do an interview and play a gig?

programme.desc: Taran wants to play football with his dad. Rajinder gives him newly invented training boots instead of playing, until he realises Taran only wants a simple kickabout.

Trevor quests to solve the mystery, but having accidentally fallen into Whizzpop’s invisibility flour, how on earth will he get everyone’s attention?

programme.title: Danger Mouse

programme.title: Super Happy Magic Forest
programme.desc: When Blossom accidentally uses a witch’s broom to make sticks for toasting marshmallows, the owner of the broom casts a spell of squeaky voices on all the heroes. The spell will be lifted once the heroes have returned with new broomstick branches. A simple enough quest, think the heroes, until they realise that a witch’s broom can only be made from the branches of the Really Spooky Tree!

programme.title: Boy Girl Dog Cat Mouse Cheese
programme.desc: While riding their scooters at the park, the bickering kids meet the Smiths. A brother and sister who don't seem to argue like our gang does - in fact, the two Smiths are super-supportive of each other! When they start pushing the other kids around, Boy, Girl, Dog, Cat, Mouse and Cheese challenge the Smiths to a race around the park! But our heroes have one problem - Cat doesn't know how to ride a scooter! The kids take turns teaching her and, when race day comes, Cat will really need to kick it into high gear if she wants to help the family beat those smug Smiths!

programme.title: Deadly 60
programme.desc: In this special episode of Deadly 60, Steve Backshall takes a deep dive into the fate of one of the most extraordinary, and endangered, ecosystems on our planet: coral reefs. They may cover less than one per cent of the ocean floor, but they support roughly a quarter of all marine life and are irreplaceable - yet they are in serious trouble. Steve travels to some of the world’s most celebrated reef systems, from the shallows of the Java Sea to the tropical waters of the Maldives. Along the way, he meets all the weird and wonderful creatures that call the reef home, including some of the best-camouflaged creatures and some impressive apex predators - he even gets a telling-off from a clownfish!

programme.title: Dennis & Gnasher Unleashed!

programme.title: Boy Girl Dog Cat Mouse Cheese
